answer: Retained Flexion closes the source-level comparison engine handoff: each grid uses exact extracted-axis keys to union period rows into one record with suffixed fields. It does not establish current purchase runtime binding, original date-offset generation or backend equivalence. Earlier unknowns are narrowed in this extension only; prior documents are preserved.

facts: Only comparison_period_criteria defines grouping identity. sort_criteria affects order and does not join rows. Fixed criteria are details_target.props; free criteria are selected condition slots in numeric order.

kl calls supplied value_extractor for each criterion in order: nil→empty string, object→JSON.stringify, other→String; joins parts with NUL. All raw rows having that key are collected regardless of period.
If comparison criteria is empty, each raw input gets a unique __row_N key. It does not align the two periods by input row index.

The key is serialization of values, not proven original SID/business identity: nil/empty and numeric/string values can collide, object property order and embedded NUL are not escaped/canonicalized by this function. No malformed/collision tests were run.

Common extractor maps $$code→code, $$date_no→data_dt$data_no, $$date_record_seq_no→data_dt$data_no$record_seq_no; otherwise raw. No relative-date offset/normalization exists in kl/Pl. Date-axis cross-period alignment therefore depends on upstream values/criteria and remains unknown.

facts: Key group rows are sorted by numeric period ascending. Each source field except __period_index is copied to field|period. Duplicate same-key same-period inputs overwrite each field with later visited values; no sum, average or Cartesian pair expansion occurs here. Earlier fields absent from a later duplicate remain.

Representative base row is last visited primary-period1 row, else first row in the sorted group. Unsuffixed fields copy that representative; model_id/index/meta are inherited from it. This is not a deep merge of both original business records.

meta.period_indices is unique observed periods sorted ascending; is_supplementary=true when period1 absent. Primary-only, compare-only and matched groups all survive the union. __period_index is not copied into merged data.
Output record remains GridBodyRow/source raw. display_index is assigned sequentially starting from first raw input index after sorting.

facts: Common chooses sort_search.sort first, else widget.attribute.sort; sorts entries by sort_seq and maps D to descending. Aggregate axis direction is separate comparison criteria.

Pl passes Ll(primaryRow,firstSortedRow,explicitSorts,axisCriteria,extractor). Ll constructs values: primary explicit values, then primary axis values, then fallback axis values when fallback object differs from primary. Missing primary yields undefined for the first two lists.

Comparator criteria array is explicitSorts followed by axisCriteria. It reads only that array length. Appended fallback-axis values in Ll are not consumed by this comparator. No fallback comparison is implied merely by constructing those extra values.

Kl uses numeric comparison only for properties definition typed Decimal/DecimalCondition/Integer: nil→0 via external Decimal, lt/gt. Other types use nil→empty string then JS string lexical < and >. No locale/natural sort. descending negates the first unequal comparison.

All compared keys equal→comparator0. No explicit tie-break on representative index or key. Before sort, groups follow first key encounter. Tie stability depends on JS Array.sort runtime semantics; no original runtime evaluation performed.
Compare-only groups can have undefined primary sort values despite actual secondary keys. Do not replace that behavior with an assumed secondary code/name sort and call it equivalent.

always_fill_body_prop_ids is a sequence-prop list from common. Those cells retain refs even in absent periods; ns keeps the unsuffixed reference for that allowlist, otherwise uses prop|period. It is not a generic zero-fill flag.

Ul accumulator skips measures if period_index not in row.meta.period_indices; included measures read nil as0 and Decimal.add. This total-stage0 default does not prove missing body cells are0. supplementary rows also interact with later Jl summary boundary handling.

manual_conditional_source_example.basis: Manual static deduction only, no original code or test/simulation executed; fabricated IDs/integers, not company data.
manual_conditional_source_example.assumptions: One nonnumeric axis k, extractor returns its raw string, no explicit sort, ascending axis, no other producer changes.
manual_conditional_source_example.sort_reason: Primary row absent for C→undefined primary axis value→empty string in Kl, sorting before A/B. Secondary C key is appended by Ll but not read by comparator. This is not observed current purchase order.
manual_conditional_source_example.missing_reason: A has no qty|2 and C has no qty|1, not injected zeroes. A same-key second primary qty9 would overwrite qty|1 to9, not add11.

implementation_blockers: Exact nonzero mode code↔year/month/week/day labels and server range-provider binding remain unknown.
Origin/comparison endpoint generation, month-end clamp/overflow, leap day, inclusive endpoints, timezone/DST and ISO/company week are not supplied by Pl/Qa.
Current purchase runtime widget/config/template/proxy path was not executed; supplier and API names are static linkage evidence only.
Original backend response groups/keys/date normalization/SID-code-name equality are unknown. Date-key matching is especially not solved by generic client equality.
Own duplicate policy or comparison-only sorting may deliberately differ from this static candidate; such choices need own-policy labels, not original parity.
Missing cell presentation, count/average/rounding, click/drilldown and print/export after all stages remain partly external.
Common full semantics OOM and Flexion full semantic timeout persist; no retries or invented semantic callable IDs.
